data.title: Erasca Reports Positive Early Data for RAS-Targeted Therapies
data.description:
The latest announcement is out from Erasca ( (ERAS) ).

On November 20, 2026, Erasca announced updated U.S. Phase 1 monotherapy and initial combination data for pan-RAS molecular glue ERAS-0015 in patients with RAS-mutant solid tumors. It also announced initial U.S. Phase 1 monotherapy data for pan-KRAS inhibitor ERAS-4001, with preliminary results supporting its potential as a combination partner for ERAS-0015.

As of the September 1, 2026, data cutoff, ERAS-0015 monotherapy at 16-32 mg once daily was generally well-tolerated and showed activity across KRAS G12X cancers. Confirmed objective response rates included 44% in 25 patients with second-line-or-later pancreatic cancer, 69% in 13 patients with KRAS G12D or G12V pancreatic cancer, 58% in 12 patients with second- or third-line non-small cell lung cancer, and 75% in four biliary tract cancer patients.

At 32 mg once daily, confirmed response rates were 63% in eight KRAS G12D pancreatic cancer patients, 80% in five KRAS G12V pancreatic cancer patients, 60% in five KRAS G12D non-small cell lung cancer patients and 50% in four KRAS G12V non-small cell lung cancer patients. Safety findings remained consistent with prior 2026 disclosures, with mostly low-grade treatment-related adverse events, no dose-limiting toxicities, and no treatment discontinuations due to treatment-related adverse events at 32 mg.

Early combination testing with gemcitabine plus nab-paclitaxel, pembrolizumab, and panitumumab was generally well-tolerated without unexpected safety signals; responses were observed in escalation cohorts with pembrolizumab and panitumumab, while efficacy data were not yet available for the gemcitabine regimen. The company said the results supported further clinical development of ERAS-0015 combinations in pancreatic, lung and colorectal cancers.

Preliminary ERAS-4001 findings showed favorable safety and tolerability, predominantly low-grade adverse events, no treatment-related adverse events leading to discontinuation, and encouraging pharmacokinetic results. Nonclinical testing found synergistic activity for the ERAS-0015 and ERAS-4001 combination in KRAS G12X-driven models, providing a rationale for further evaluation.

data.title: Bath & Body Works Earnings Call Signals Cautious Recovery
data.description:
Bath & Body Works, Inc. ((BBWI)) has held its Q3 earnings call. Read on for the main highlights of the call.

Bath & Body Works delivered a cautiously optimistic quarter, beating its sales and earnings guidance despite a year-over-year sales decline. Digital, international, innovation, customer engagement, and cost savings improved, but store traffic, body care, seasonal execution, tariffs, and competition remained significant challenges.

Third-Quarter Results Beat Expectations

Bath & Body Works reported third-quarter net sales of approximately $1.6 billion, down 1% from a year earlier but ahead of its guidance range. Adjusted earnings per diluted share reached $0.26, exceeding the projected range of $0.07 to $0.12.

Digital Business Returned to Growth

Digital sales grew for a second straight quarter, supported by better conversion and gains among new, existing, and reactivated customers. The company also completed a website relaunch featuring richer storytelling, AI-powered browsing, and personalized product recommendations.

New Product Franchises Gained Traction

Essentials, Everyday Luxuries, Reserve, and Fruit Fusion each generated positive customer responses and mid-single-digit sales growth. The franchises achieved planned premium pricing, while customers who bought them returned at rates above the company average.

Essentials Drove Repeat Purchases

Essentials sales exceeded management’s expectations during the quarter. More than half of Essentials buyers returned to shop within 30 days, a repeat-purchase rate significantly above the broader brand average.

Everyday Luxuries Sales Nearly Doubled

Retail sales of the reimagined Everyday Luxuries collection approximately doubled from the comparable period last year. New formats such as rollerballs and eau de parfum added sales without reducing demand for core fine fragrance mists.

International Growth Remained Strong

International retail sales rose at a low-double-digit rate year over year in the third quarter. Performance benefited from new store and market openings, as well as improved shipping capabilities into the Middle East.

Expanded Distribution Continued to Build Momentum

Amazon and Ulta posted improving sales trends and attracted encouraging numbers of new customers. Ulta will expand Bath & Body Works’ holiday assortment to about 1,500 stores from roughly 600, with Pink Suede launching exclusively through the channel.

Wholesale and International Revenue Climbed

International and other net sales, including expanded-distribution wholesale revenue, reached $101 million, up approximately 39% from last year. The business contributed about 190 basis points of overall company growth during the quarter.

Direct Channel Sales Increased

Direct channel net sales rose approximately 3% year over year to $307 million. The gain reflects continued progress in digital and other direct customer relationships, even as company-operated store sales remained under pressure.

Marketing and Customer Trends Improved

The company increased marketing investment and reported healthier trends among new, existing, and reactivated customers. Existing customers delivered their strongest quarter of the year, while retention and reactivation improved particularly in digital.

Brand Campaigns Showed Early Progress

The Season of Wonder and A Thousand Wishes campaigns improved brand metrics, including brand love and perceptions of ingredient quality. A Thousand Wishes became one of the company’s strongest social posts of the year, while TikTok delivered encouraging gains in brand awareness.

Creator Marketing Lifted Engagement

Bath & Body Works is developing relationships with thousands of creators to broaden its reach. Early results showed creator content producing click-through rates well above those generated by branded content.

Cost Savings Exceeded the Annual Goal

The company expects to deliver approximately $200 million in Fuel for Growth savings this year, beating its $175 million target by about $25 million. The savings are funding product innovation, marketing, digital capabilities, and expansion into new channels.

Gross and Merchandise Margins Beat Guidance

Third-quarter adjusted gross profit margin was 40.8%, about 50 basis points below last year but above guidance. Adjusted merchandise margin improved approximately 30 basis points, helped by favorable physical inventory results and the timing of Canadian tariff expense.

Cash Flow Supported Shareholder Returns

Bath & Body Works expects approximately $600 million of fiscal 2026 free cash flow. It paid $40 million in dividends, repurchased 3.4 million shares for $60 million, authorized a new $500 million buyback program, and repurchased and extinguished $250 million of notes.

Store Expansion Continued

The company opened 24 stores, mainly in off-mall locations, while international partners opened 29. Bath & Body Works ended the quarter with 1,959 North American company-owned stores and 623 international locations, including its first three stores using a new design concept.

New Store Experiences Showed Promise

Early results from the redesigned store concepts were encouraging. An eau de parfum bar resonated with shoppers and supported fragrance sales, while a digital scent finder proved effective as a selling tool.

Sales Still Declined Year Over Year

Despite exceeding its forecast, third-quarter net sales fell 1% to approximately $1.6 billion. Management acknowledged that the underlying business remained pressured, highlighting the gap between beating a lowered outlook and returning to strong growth.

U.S. and Canadian Stores Fell 4%

U.S. and Canadian store net sales declined 4% to approximately $1.2 billion. Management cited weak traffic, a channel shift linked to the Free Ship 50 offer, and a more challenging consumer environment.

Traffic, Inflation, and Competition Weighed

Retail traffic remained weak as inflation continued to affect consumer spending and competition intensified across core categories. Management said conditions became more pressured toward the latter part of the third quarter.

Halloween Missed Expectations

Halloween performance fell short and became a significant headwind for the quarter. Management attributed the result to an unsuccessful collection and acknowledged that the company had temporarily lost focus on seasonal execution.

Body Care Remained a Weak Spot

Body care performed well below expectations, although results were consistent with the second quarter. Management said the category is especially competitive, with changing consumer expectations and stronger competition making improvement more difficult.

Seasonal Results Were Uneven

The Preserve and Nightmare Before Christmas collections performed well, but overall seasonal execution was mixed. Management said it must improve assortment, presentation, and storytelling across each seasonal event.

Product Availability Limited Innovation Sales

Some new products sold faster than planned, leaving the company unable to meet all available demand. Management identified better product availability as a priority for capturing the full benefit of its innovation pipeline.

Company Stores Remained Below Target

Management said company-owned stores remain central to the brand but are not yet performing at the desired level. Conversion improved, although the business still needs to give shoppers stronger reasons to visit stores.

Holiday Outlook Stayed Cautious

The holiday period remains the company’s most important selling season, but traffic is under pressure and competition is expected to be intense. The current model assumes average unit retail prices will be roughly flat with last year, while management is prepared to compete more aggressively if needed.

Fourth-Quarter and Full-Year Guidance

For the fourth quarter, Bath & Body Works expects sales to decline 5.5% to 2%, a gross profit rate near 42.4%, and adjusted earnings per share of $1.41 to $1.61. Full-year sales guidance improved to a decline of 3.4% to 2.1%, while adjusted earnings per share remained at $2.60 to $2.80.

Margins Face Tariff and Oil Pressure

Fourth-quarter merchandise margin is expected to face more than 200 basis points of pressure from new tariffs and higher merchandise input costs. Tariffs are expected to create a headwind of well over one point, while crude oil is projected to add approximately another point of pressure.

Management Targets Sustainable Growth

The company expects about $200 million in Fuel for Growth savings, approximately $215 million in capital spending, and roughly $600 million in free cash flow for fiscal 2026. Management’s longer-term goal is to return the business to sustainable growth in 2027, with new products reaching a high-single-digit share of global retail sales.

Bath & Body Works’ earnings call showed meaningful progress in digital, international, innovation, and cost control, but the recovery remains incomplete. Investors will likely focus on whether stronger customer engagement and new products can offset weak stores, uneven seasonal execution, competitive pressure, and rising costs.

data.title: Construction Partners’ Earnings Call Signals Strong Growth
data.description:
Construction Partners ((ROAD)) has held its Q4 earnings call. Read on for the main highlights of the call.

Construction Partners’ Earnings Call Signals Strong Growth

Construction Partners delivered a strongly positive earnings call, highlighting record fiscal 2026 results, strong organic and acquisitive expansion, and a sizable backlog. Management acknowledged weather disruption, higher diesel costs, lower margins and elevated leverage, but described each issue as manageable while emphasizing the company’s continued growth investments.

Record Fiscal 2026 Performance

Construction Partners reported fiscal 2026 revenue of $3.674 billion, up 31% year over year, while net income rose 40% to $142.1 million. Adjusted EBITDA increased 24% to $523.5 million, adjusted net income climbed 27% to $154.5 million, and gross profit grew approximately 27% to $558.8 million.

Organic Growth and Platform Expansion

Organic revenue growth reached 6.9% during fiscal 2026, supported by expansion across the company’s Sunbelt footprint. Construction Partners also completed seven acquisitions in four high-growth states, opened four greenfield locations and strengthened its local market positions.

Acquisition Activity Continues

The company completed three more acquisitions during the first 35 days of fiscal 2027, underscoring management’s continued appetite for expansion. Completed deals are expected to add roughly $280 million to $300 million of fiscal 2027 revenue, including approximately $100 million to $110 million from the three newest transactions.

Backlog Provides Revenue Visibility

Project backlog stood at approximately $3.29 billion at September 30, 2026, supporting management’s revenue outlook. About 75% to 80% of the next 12 months’ contract revenue is covered, while the latest acquisitions added $65 million of backlog expected to convert substantially into fiscal 2027 revenue.

Healthy Sunbelt Market Conditions

Management described economic activity and bidding opportunities across its Sunbelt markets as healthy, although conditions vary by location and project type. Growing taxpayer bases and dedicated state revenue sources continue to support transportation programs across the company’s eight states.

Diversified Model Supports Project Selection

Construction Partners’ crews can shift between public and commercial work, allowing local businesses to pursue the most attractive projects across several end markets. Management said this flexibility helps the company prioritize work with better margins and respond to changing demand.

Data Centers Offer Selective Opportunity

Data centers were described as attractive, good-margin opportunities when they overlap with the company’s existing operations. Construction Partners is working on several projects in Texas and negotiating additional work, though the timing, location and broader economic impact of future projects remain uncertain.

Progress Toward ROAD 2030

The ROAD 2030 plan targets approximately $6 billion in annual revenue and $1 billion in Adjusted EBITDA by fiscal 2030. The strategy calls for an Adjusted EBITDA margin of about 17%, supported by organic growth, greenfield facilities and disciplined acquisitions.

G&A Efficiency and Cash Flow Improve

General and administrative expenses declined to 7% of revenue in fiscal 2026 from 7.1% a year earlier, showing modest operating leverage. Cash flow from operations rose 18% to $344 million, giving the company additional resources to support its expansion plans.

Liquidity Supports Investment

Construction Partners ended fiscal 2026 with $132.9 million of cash and cash equivalents and $480.3 million available under its credit facility after outstanding letters of credit. Management expects fiscal 2027 capital spending of $210 million to $230 million, including maintenance spending and high-return growth investments.

Acquisitions Funded With Discipline

Fiscal 2026 acquisition purchases totaled approximately $477 million, while about $280 million of debt was added to the balance sheet. Nearly $200 million was funded through cash and stock, and management said it remains engaged in discussions with sellers rather than pausing its acquisition program.

Recent Deals Broaden Capabilities

Roads, Inc. increased market share in Pensacola, while Asphalt Express supports development of a fourth terminal in Ardmore. Cline Construction added site-work capabilities and a rail terminal on Florida’s east coast, and Piedmont expanded the company’s position south of metro Atlanta.

Texas Expansion Gains Momentum

Within two years of entering Texas, Construction Partners expanded into Austin, San Antonio, Belton, Houston and Abilene. Management said the state’s growth should continue to support transportation infrastructure activity regardless of whether its administration is Democratic or Republican.

Federal Funding Outlook Is Constructive

Management expects Congress ultimately to approve and increase funding through a new multi-year surface transportation bill. Although the timing of reauthorization remains uncertain, the company does not expect a disruption to fiscal 2027 funding or project activity and views a continuing resolution as manageable.

Diesel Pass-Through Could Aid Margins

Diesel costs rose 40% beginning in the second week of August, creating a significant fourth-quarter burden. Construction Partners began passing the increase through immediately and expects the model to work similarly to 2022, with margins recovering during the second half of fiscal 2027.

Seasonal Backlog Decline Was Normal

The company converted $924 million of project revenue in the fourth quarter, its largest quarterly burn on record. Management said a sequential decline in fourth-quarter backlog is normal because backlog typically falls during the summer and rebuilds during the winter.

Winter Purchases May Lower Energy Costs

Construction Partners expects to continue buying liquid materials during the winter, when demand is lower and refinery supply is more favorable. Management said these purchases typically provide discounted pricing and can benefit the company for two or three months into the construction season.

Employee Culture Remains a Strength

Management credited approximately 7,700 employees for the company’s organic growth, backlog development and safe operations. It also said the culture helps Construction Partners remain an acquirer of choice while improving its ability to attract and retain construction talent.

Adjusted EBITDA Margin Declined

Fiscal 2026 Adjusted EBITDA margin fell to 14.2% from 15.1% in fiscal 2025, reflecting pressure from input costs, weather and project timing. Management cautioned that margins can fluctuate based on acquisition mix and the timing of work, rather than following a straight-line path.

Weather Disrupted the Fourth Quarter

Very wet conditions in July and during the first week of August delayed construction activity and represented the largest fourth-quarter impact. September brought some recovery, but unfinished work shifted into the following quarter instead of being completed on schedule.

Energy Costs Remain Volatile

The 40% diesel price increase beginning in August weighed heavily on fourth-quarter results and left energy costs entering fiscal 2027 above prior-year levels. Management’s immediate pass-through actions are intended to limit the longer-term effect on profitability.

Newer Acquisitions Start With Lower Margins

Several acquisitions completed during the previous six months initially carried lower-margin backlogs than the Texas businesses acquired earlier. Management said the gap is not dramatic and expects margins to improve during the first year as the acquired backlog is replaced with higher-margin work.

Leverage Remains Above Target

The company ended fiscal 2026 with a consolidated net leverage ratio of 3.24 times, above management’s long-term objective of approximately 2.5 times. Reducing leverage remains an important financial priority as Construction Partners continues to balance acquisitions, capital spending and growth.

Backlog Coverage Is Below Recent Peaks

The 75% to 80% coverage of the next 12 months’ contract revenue is below the 80% to 85% levels seen in recent years. Management characterized the figure as roughly midrange historically, noting that coverage had typically been closer to 60% to 70% for a longer period.

Federal Reauthorization Timing Unclear

Management said it does not have visibility into when federal transportation reauthorization will be completed. Despite that uncertainty, Construction Partners does not expect the process to interrupt fiscal 2027 funding or project activity.

Market Conditions Differ Across Regions

The overall Sunbelt environment remains favorable, but management stressed that local conditions vary by market and project type. This variation makes the company’s geographic reach and ability to shift crews between end markets important competitive advantages.

First-Half Seasonality Remains Significant

Management expects the first half of fiscal 2027 to generate approximately 40% to 42% of annual revenue and 33% to 35% of Adjusted EBITDA. The lower profit contribution reflects the seasonal weighting of the company’s geographic footprint and construction activity.

Fiscal 2027 Guidance Reiterated

Construction Partners expects fiscal 2027 revenue of $4.175 billion to $4.275 billion, net income of $170.9 million to $180.8 million and adjusted net income of $174.6 million to $185.4 million. Adjusted EBITDA is projected at $585 million to $620 million, with a margin of 14% to 14.5% and organic revenue growth of 6% to 8%.

Management also expects $210 million to $230 million of fiscal 2027 capital expenditures and continued acquisition contributions of $280 million to $300 million. Longer term, the company remains focused on approximately $6 billion of annual revenue, $1 billion of Adjusted EBITDA, a 17% margin by fiscal 2030 and net leverage near 2.5 times.

Construction Partners’ earnings call presented a company growing rapidly across attractive Sunbelt markets while managing weather, energy and balance-sheet challenges. Record results, strong backlog, acquisition activity and reiterated guidance support the bullish outlook, though investors will be watching margin recovery and leverage reduction closely.

data.title: Magnera Earnings Call Shows Progress Amid Demand Pressures
data.description:
Magnera Corporation ((MAGN)) has held its Q4 earnings call. Read on for the main highlights of the call.

Magnera Earnings Call Signals Progress Despite Uneven Demand

Magnera’s earnings call carried a broadly positive tone, supported by year-over-year earnings growth, strong free cash flow, debt reduction and progress on merger synergies. Management also pointed to product innovation and operational gains, although softer volumes, European and Chinese headwinds, inflation, an impairment charge and leverage above target remain important risks.

Synergies and Project CORE Advance

Magnera said it has delivered its synergy savings commitment to date, with the remaining value expected in fiscal 2027. Project CORE actions across Argentina, the U.K. and France have expanded into a broader business-excellence platform.

Transition Services Agreement Completed

The company exited its transition services agreement with Amcor on schedule. Magnera migrated 11 enterprise-resource-planning systems across 10 manufacturing sites and one technical center, marking a major integration milestone.

Safety Performance Improves

Magnera reduced its incident rate by 18% compared with 2025. Management said the result places the company among industry leaders for safety performance.

Earnings Continue to Grow

Quarterly earnings increased 8% from the prior-year period, while full-year results were nearly 4% higher. The improvement reflects synergy capture, productivity gains and stronger execution across the business.

Cash Flow Supports Debt Reduction

Magnera generated $115 million of free cash flow in fiscal 2026 and reduced debt by $122 million. That included a $57 million repayment in the fourth quarter, reinforcing management’s focus on balance-sheet improvement.

Innovation Supports Organic Growth

The company reported solid organic growth in global wipes and infrastructure products. New and expanded offerings include HighPleat filtration media, improved food-packaging absorbency, the Universa industrial wipes platform and softer, pH-neutral personal-care products.

Two-Year Cash Flow Record

Since launching its current strategy two years ago, Magnera has generated more than $240 million of free cash flow. Management said free cash flow yield has remained above 25% relative to period-end market capitalization.

Liquidity Provides Strategic Flexibility

Magnera ended fiscal 2026 with approximately $600 million of available liquidity. The resources give the company capacity to fund strategic investments while pursuing selected growth opportunities.

Americas Segment Delivers Profit Growth

Americas revenue rose 2% year over year, helped by pricing actions and continued strength in infrastructure-related construction markets. Adjusted EBITDA increased 7% to $65 million, supported by Project CORE, synergies and manufacturing productivity.

Rest of World Profitability Improves

Rest of World revenue increased 1%, as pricing and continued wipes strength partly offset weaker European demand. Adjusted EBITDA rose 10% to $33 million despite a 6% organic volume decline.

Strategic Capital Investment Planned

Magnera expects to invest approximately $85 million in fiscal 2027 capital spending. The company is prioritizing consumer-solutions markets where it believes its differentiated products provide a strong competitive position.

German Production Line Comes Online

A new high-performance blown-film line has been installed and commissioned at Magnera’s Dombühl, Germany, site. Commercial orders are expected to be produced and shipped in the first calendar quarter of 2027.

Core End Markets Remain Stable

Adult incontinence and feminine-care products sold through retail and away-from-home channels were described as stable. Management also cited continued demand strength in wipes and infrastructure-related applications.

Commercial and Operational Systems Standardized

Magnera has integrated its commercial teams to provide more consistent customer service. It is also standardizing operational metrics and processes while implementing efficiency initiatives across the organization.

Innovation Portfolio Expands

The company’s Vitality Index, which tracks newer products, rose to nearly 30% of the portfolio from 22% when tracking began. Management said the increase supports more innovation projects and potential investment in attractive end-use markets.

Utilization Creates Investment Opportunities

Some regional platforms are approaching utilization rates in the mid-90% range, while longer supply-demand markets are operating in the 80s. Management said utilization is moving in the right direction and could support targeted investment.

Early Contract Talks Are Encouraging

Management said early signals from the fiscal 2027 bid season were positive and that negotiations were progressing on a normal timetable. Customer service and product quality are supporting the discussions, although final outcomes remain dependent on market conditions.

Productivity Benefits Continue

Fiscal 2027 includes approximately $20 million of rollover benefits from actions taken in fiscal 2026, compared with about $45 million of benefit in fiscal 2026. Additional Project CORE actions are included in the $400 million EBITDA midpoint.

Europe and China Remain Headwinds

Management expects Europe and China to remain exposed to economic disruption and geopolitical pressure. Those conditions are expected to restrain volume growth and contribute to a broadly flat Rest of World outlook.

Energy and Inflation Pressure Margins

Fiscal 2027 assumptions include approximately $10 million of European energy inflation, along with other inflationary pressures. Magnera said it was about 70% hedged for European energy and still needed to close part of the remaining gap.

Fourth-Quarter Volume Was Softer

Although earnings were consistent with prior expectations, volume was weaker than anticipated late in the fourth quarter. European order pushouts, softness in selected categories and continued customer inventory rebalancing affected results.

Americas Health Care Demand Weakens

Softer health care demand produced a 2% net organic decline in the Americas during the quarter. The weakness limited the benefit from pricing and strength in infrastructure-related markets.

Rest of World Volumes Decline

Rest of World organic volume fell 6%, primarily because of weaker demand in parts of Europe. Pricing actions and wipes strength helped protect revenue and earnings despite the volume pressure.

Limited Volume Growth Expected

Management described the fiscal 2027 volume outlook as low-single-digit growth in the Americas and slightly low-single-digit negative to flat in Europe. The midpoint assumes flat global volume, while the EBITDA range reflects scenarios from 2% lower to 2% higher volume.

Inventory Volatility Remains Elevated

Magnera described the operating environment as unlikely to return to normal soon. Management expects continued quarter-to-quarter inventory swings, including customer pullbacks, sudden snapbacks and occasional heavy pull-ins or panic orders.

Leverage Remains Above Target

At the midpoint of its fiscal 2027 free cash flow outlook, Magnera expects to direct approximately $120 million toward debt reduction. That would bring leverage to roughly 3.6x, still above the company’s long-term target of 3x.

Cash Flow Is Weighted to the Second Half

Fiscal 2027 free cash flow is expected to be stronger in the back half of the year. Management plans inventory actions in the first quarter to establish appropriate stock levels after inventory positioning proved insufficient in the prior year.

Impairment Charge Weighs on Results

Magnera recorded a $106 million impairment charge in the quarter. Management attributed the primary pressure to the company’s internal carrying value compared with fair value, including the market multiple relative to the multiple at the inception of the RMT.

Foreign Exchange Offsets Shipping Benefit

Extra shipping days are expected to provide a $5 million to $6 million benefit in fiscal 2027. Management said a foreign-exchange headwind is likely to offset that gain and could be slightly larger than the shipping-day benefit.

Capacity and Demand Remain Uncertain

Magnera and competitors have removed capacity from the market, but available capacity remains in certain platforms and regions. Management also described global demand as uncertain, including demand in spun-melt applications.

Lower-Margin Work Is Being Rationalized

Some volume softness reflected decisions to exit or avoid activities where Magnera was not receiving sufficient value for its products. The approach may reduce near-term volume but is intended to improve business quality and returns.

Project CORE Benefits Are Becoming Less Direct

Management said the cost-to-EBITDA relationship from the next Project CORE extension is not as close to one-for-one as it was during the first wave of actions. This suggests future benefits may require more operational execution and investment.

Fiscal 2027 Guidance

Magnera expects comparable EBITDA of approximately $400 million at the fiscal 2027 midpoint, representing about 6% growth on a constant-currency basis. Free cash flow is expected at $110 million to $130 million, weighted toward the back half, with approximately $85 million of capital investment and about $120 million directed to debt reduction at the midpoint.

Outlook Balances Growth and Risk

The guidance assumes flat global volume, low-single-digit growth in the Americas and flat to slightly negative volume in Europe. It also incorporates about $125 million of cash interest, $50 million of tax integration costs, $20 million of additional Project CORE items, 10% to 11% cash taxes as a share of EBITDA, 70% European energy hedging and a $5 million to $6 million shipping-day benefit.

Magnera’s call showed a company making measurable progress on synergies, cash generation, safety and innovation while navigating uneven demand. The fiscal 2027 outlook points to moderate EBITDA growth and further debt reduction, but leverage, European conditions, inventory swings and limited volume growth remain key issues for investors.

data.title: Alibaba Earnings Call: AI Growth Outpaces Rising Investment
data.description:
Alibaba Group ((BABA)) has held its Q2 earnings call. Read on for the main highlights of the call.

Alibaba’s earnings call struck a strongly positive tone, led by faster revenue growth, a sharp increase in profit, and sustained momentum in AI cloud services. Management also acknowledged pressure from export controls, weaker consumption, heavy infrastructure spending, and negative free cash flow, but investors were left with a broadly favorable view of the company’s operating progress.

Revenue and Profit Accelerate

Alibaba’s total revenue rose 10% year over year to CNY 272 billion. Adjusted EBITDA surged 260% to CNY 32.6 billion, while adjusted EBITDA margin reached 14.5% and GAAP net income jumped 213% to CNY 64.4 billion.

Cash Flow and Net Cash Strengthen

Operating cash flow increased 55% to CNY 15.7 billion, showing stronger cash generation from the core business. As of September 30, 2026, net cash stood at $32.9 billion, up from $30.7 billion in the prior quarter, or about $49 billion excluding long-dated debt.

AI Cloud Growth Remains Rapid

External AI cloud and compute revenue climbed 64% year over year, marking the tenth straight quarter of accelerating growth. Total AI cloud and compute revenue rose 53% to CNY 61 billion, including CNY 47 billion from external customers.

Recurring Cloud Revenue Expands

Recurring revenue from external cloud customers increased 67% to CNY 37 billion. Adjusted EBITDA rose 121%, while margins expanded to about 14.5% in management’s overview and 14.9% in the segment update.

AI Products Become a Cloud Pillar

AI-related product revenue reached CNY 17.9 billion, representing 49% of Alibaba Cloud’s external recurring revenue. The business delivered triple-digit growth for the thirteenth consecutive quarter, with its annual revenue run rate exceeding $10 billion.

Demand Spreads Across AI Markets

Alibaba reported broad demand from AI laboratories for training and inference services. Customers also included state-owned enterprises and businesses in manufacturing, automotive, biotechnology, storage, security, networking, and core processor services.

T-Head Advances Chip Commercialization

T-Head’s Zhenwu M890-powered supernode instances are ramping in volume and moving into commercial-scale deployment. The company’s next-generation V900 is designed to deliver three times the M890’s computing performance, while the J900 remains part of the longer-term chip roadmap.

Domestic Chips Support Alibaba Models

Alibaba’s Qwen is already training its next-generation model on T-Head domestic chips, while Model Studio offers inference on the same technology. Management said current chips can support large and ultra-large models, strengthening the role of domestic hardware in Alibaba’s AI infrastructure.

Long-Term Cloud Targets Reaffirmed

Alibaba reaffirmed its calendar 2030 goal of generating $100 billion in external cloud revenue with a margin above 20%. Management said enterprise adoption, deeper AI integration, proprietary chips, and full-stack capabilities should support that ambition.

Qwen Expands Its AI Ecosystem

The Qwen4-Max foundation model contains 2.4 trillion backbone parameters and is positioned as a leading model for agentic tasks and coding. Alibaba also highlighted QwenWork, QwenWork E-Commerce, and a Qwen app offering services across more than 20 daily-life use cases.

AI Applications Grow While Losses Narrow

Revenue from AI laboratories and applications rose 51% to CNY 4.4 billion, driven mainly by demand for agentic AI products. The segment’s loss narrowed quarter over quarter to CNY 10.5 billion as model-training efficiency improved and Qwen app marketing spending became more disciplined.

E-Commerce Profitability Improves

Alibaba’s E-Commerce Group adjusted EBITDA rose 243% to CNY 38.9 billion. The gain was driven primarily by a substantial reduction in China quick-commerce losses, while domestic commerce remained profitable, international losses declined, and global wholesale delivered strong profits.

Quick Commerce Shows Better Economics

China quick-commerce revenue increased 22% to CNY 58.8 billion, supported by strong Freshippo growth online and in stores. Non-food online gross merchandise value rose more than 40%, while stable market share, higher order values, and improving unit economics helped narrow losses.

Quick Commerce Moves Toward Profitability

Management said quick-commerce losses should continue to narrow in the December quarter. Alibaba remains committed to halving losses next year and achieving profitability in instant retail by fiscal 2029.

B2B and Xianyu Continue to Advance

Alibaba integrated its international and domestic B2B operations to connect overseas demand with domestic supply more effectively. Xianyu, the company’s secondhand marketplace, delivered 29% order growth while remaining profitable during the quarter.

Cloud Margins Gain Several Tailwinds

Margin expansion reflected a larger share of high-margin recurring revenue, pricing benefits from tight compute supply, data-center scale efficiencies, and proprietary chips. Alibaba Cloud now operates 109 availability zones across 32 regions, with facilities in the Netherlands, France, and Brazil coming online progressively.

T-Head Files for a Potential Listing

T-Head confidentially submitted a listing application to regulators, a step that could give greater visibility to Alibaba’s chip business. Management said domestic compute is becoming a larger part of Alibaba Cloud’s capacity and described the shift as structurally positive for the cloud segment.

AI Infrastructure Investment Continues

Alibaba plans to keep investing in AI infrastructure to extend its competitive lead and strengthen its long-term position. Management also emphasized discipline, saying capital allocation would remain focused on returns on invested capital and proactive cash management.

Export Controls Weigh on Cloud Outlook

New compute export-control rules are expected to affect products and services next year, while supply-chain uncertainty remains elevated. Management said cloud growth could slow before recovering as domestic compute products scale.

Alibaba May Reduce Its 20 GW Target

The company’s preliminary assessment is that changing global compute policies could lead to a downward revision of its long-term 20 GW data-center and compute target. Such a change would also affect the scale of Alibaba’s overall capital expenditure plan.

Capital Spending Drives Negative Free Cash Flow

Capital expenditure reached CNY 50.5 billion, or $7.5 billion, as Alibaba expanded AI capacity, absorbed higher chip-component prices, and increased CPU capacity for expected AI-agent demand. Free cash flow was negative CNY 34.5 billion, compared with negative CNY 21.8 billion a year earlier.

Investment Cycle Remains Extended

Management expects the most sustained investment period to cover the first half of 2027 and 2028, with domestic-chip spending particularly intense during those years. The company expects overall cash flow to turn positive in the second half of 2028.

Chinese Consumers Remain Cautious

Alibaba said domestic consumption remained under pressure in the December quarter, with consumers becoming more careful and some categories facing intense competition. Consumer staples showed healthier growth than discretionary products, highlighting uneven demand across the market.

Commerce Marketing Revenue Declines

China commerce customer-management revenue fell 5% year over year. On a like-for-like basis, excluding the contra-revenue effect of a new business-development program, the measure grew 1%.

Other Businesses Face Revenue and Investment Pressure

Revenue in the all-other segment declined 5% to CNY 27.7 billion, mainly because of lower Cainiao revenue. The segment posted an adjusted EBITDA loss of CNY 3.3 billion as Alibaba increased investment in technology businesses.

Model Releases Lag Expectations

Management acknowledged that model launches from Alibaba and its partners had been somewhat slower than expected over the preceding two months. Despite that timing issue, the company maintained its full-year MaaS annual recurring revenue target of CNY 30 billion after launching Qwen4.

Regulatory Effects Remain Unclear

New regulations covering compute power and access are still being implemented, making their impact difficult to measure. Alibaba said it was too early to determine how the rules could affect model training and the speed of future model iterations.

Forward Guidance and Investment Outlook

Alibaba kept its 2030 targets of $100 billion in external cloud revenue and a margin above 20%, while expecting cloud growth of 30% to 45% next year before recovering to 50% or more in 2028. Management also outlined V900 mass production in early 2027, commercial supernodes later that year, narrowing quick-commerce losses, positive overall cash flow in late 2028, and instant-retail profitability by fiscal 2029.

Alibaba’s results showed that AI is becoming a powerful growth and profit engine across the group. Although export restrictions, softer consumption, heavy capital spending, and near-term cash outflows remain important risks, stronger cloud economics, improving e-commerce profitability, and reaffirmed long-term targets support an optimistic earnings-call takeaway.

data.title: Courtside Group Earnings Call Highlights PodcastOne Growth
data.description:
Courtside Group Inc ((PODC)) has held its Q2 earnings call. Read on for the main highlights of the call.

The call presented a broadly positive picture for Courtside Group’s PodcastOne business, with revenue growth, stronger adjusted EBITDA and narrower operating and net losses. Management also pointed to audience momentum, new programming, expanded distribution and continued investment in technology, although the company remains unprofitable.

Revenue Reached $15.4 Million

PodcastOne reported fiscal 2027 second-quarter revenue of $15.4 million, providing a foundation for its improved profitability measures. The result reflects continued activity across its content, distribution and advertising operations.

Adjusted EBITDA Increased

Adjusted EBITDA rose to $1.4 million from $1.1 million in the same year-ago quarter. Management attributed the improvement to revenue growth and better contribution margins, signaling progress in the company’s operating model.

Operating Loss Narrowed

The second-quarter operating loss fell to $500,000 from $1 million a year earlier. Courtside Group said higher revenue and lower stock-based compensation in general and administrative expenses were the main drivers of the improvement.

Net Loss and Per-Share Loss Improved

Net loss declined to $500,000, or $0.02 per basic and diluted share, compared with a $1 million loss, or $0.04 per share, in the prior-year quarter. The improvement shows better financial performance, though the business has not yet reached profitability.

PodcastOne Earned a Top-Eight Ranking

PodcastOne ranked No. 8 in Podtrac’s U.S. podcast publisher rankings for September. Management presented the result as evidence that the network remains a significant player in the competitive podcast market.

Premium Entertainment Portfolio Expanded

The company secured a multiyear agreement for exclusive sales and distribution rights to “Dropping Names…and Other Things with Brent & Jonny.” Hosted by Brent Spiner and Jonathan Frakes, the program adds an established entertainment franchise and creates opportunities for audience growth and advertising partnerships.

New Acquired and Original Shows Added

PodcastOne expanded its lineup through the acquisition of “FluentlyForward,” hosted by Shannon McNamara, and the launch of “People Pleasers.” The original series, hosted by Leah Rudick and Jessica Michelle Singleton, broadens the company’s comedy, lifestyle, relationship, entertainment and self-improvement offerings.

The Prosecutors Built Audience Momentum

“The Prosecutors” attracted strong interest through real-time coverage of the Lindsay Clancy case. Hosts Alice and Brett also increased the show’s visibility through media appearances, including spots on “Crime Stories with Nancy Grace.”

A&E and PAVE Distribution Expanded

PodcastOne continued distributing programs through partnerships with PAVE Studios and A&E, including “The First 48” and “History’s Greatest Mysteries.” Management also cited “Celebrity Ghost Stories,” “The Unbelievable” and “The UnXplained,” with cross-promotion and targeted feed drops supporting engagement.

Redesigned Website Targets Discovery

PodcastOne launched a redesigned website to make shows easier to find and improve the listener experience. The platform is also intended to support search engine optimization and attract more listeners through organic audience growth.

Creator and Audience Development Continued

Management said the company continued investing in audience expansion and creator development. It is also working to give talent more opportunities across audio, video and social media, reflecting the changing ways audiences consume content.

AI Infrastructure Supported Operations

PodcastOne continued developing artificial intelligence tools for predictive profitability, advertising management, audio quality and search visibility. Other applications include advertising attribution, short-form video creation, talent identification and analysis of audience interests.

Advertising and Analytics Capabilities Grew

The company invested in advertising technology, audience analytics and programmatic infrastructure. These tools are designed to help connect brands with engaged listeners and provide more measurable advertising results.

Content Has Multiplatform Potential

Management highlighted opportunities to extend programming across traditional audio, YouTube, social media and major streaming services. As video becomes more important to podcast discovery and consumption, the company sees additional ways to expand the reach and value of its content.

Focus Remained on Intellectual Property

Courtside Group is continuing to build creator relationships, develop original intellectual property and strengthen distribution and advertising capabilities. Partnerships with A&E and PAVE Studios also allow the company to leverage established programming while pursuing broader commercial opportunities.

Podcast Advertising Trends Stayed Favorable

Management cited industry research showing that video, major streaming platforms and new discovery channels are increasingly important to advertisers. The company also emphasized the value of highly engaged podcast listeners, saying these trends continue to support the podcast advertising model.

Operating Loss Remained Negative

Despite improving from $1 million to $500,000 year over year, PodcastOne still recorded an operating loss in the quarter. The result underscores that stronger revenue and margins have not yet fully covered the company’s operating costs.

Net Loss Continued

PodcastOne remained unprofitable, reporting a $500,000 net loss and a $0.02 loss per basic and diluted share. While both measures improved from the prior year, investors will continue watching for evidence of a sustained move toward positive earnings.

Management’s Fiscal 2027 Priorities

For the remainder of fiscal 2027, management said it will focus on expanding creator relationships, strengthening distribution and advertising capabilities, and developing valuable intellectual property. The company did not provide specific numerical guidance for revenue, operating loss, net loss, adjusted EBITDA or other financial measures.

The earnings call combined improving financial results with an aggressive content and technology strategy. Courtside Group’s PodcastOne business is gaining scale and visibility, but continued losses mean execution and progress toward consistent profitability remain central issues for investors.

data.title: StoneX Earnings Call Highlights Record Growth and Challenges
data.description:
Stonex Group Inc. ((SNEX)) has held its Q4 earnings call. Read on for the main highlights of the call.

StoneX delivered a strongly positive earnings call, powered by record fiscal 2026 profit, revenue, earnings per share and return on equity. Management also highlighted strong commercial and payments growth, a largely completed R.J. O’Brien integration and expanding AI capabilities, although the fourth quarter faced weaker institutional and retail activity, lower client-float income and higher taxes.

Record Fiscal 2026 Results

StoneX reported record fiscal 2026 net income of $525.4 million, up 72% from the prior year, while operating revenue rose 44% to $5.9 billion. Diluted EPS increased 58% to $4.15, with return on equity at 19.5% and return on tangible equity at 26.9%.

Fourth-Quarter Revenue Growth

Fourth-quarter net operating revenue increased 12% year over year to $655 million, while pretax net income rose 10% to nearly $120 million. Total segment income grew 13% to $328 million, showing continued operating momentum despite uneven market conditions.

Book Value and Equity Expansion

Closing book value per share rose 20% year over year to $24.24. Stockholders’ equity increased 72% over two years, and the company exceeded its 15% return-on-equity target.

R.J. O’Brien Integration Advances

StoneX completed nearly all R.J. O’Brien client migrations on schedule and achieved an expense-synergy exit run rate of $55 million, above its target of more than $50 million. Capital synergies reached $70 million versus a $50 million goal, reinforcing the strategic value of the acquisition.

Commercial Segment Leads Growth

Commercial net operating revenue jumped 54% to $334 million, while segment income rose 66% to $188 million. The segment margin improved from 52% to 56%, and full-year revenue and income increased 76% and 97%, respectively.

Physical and OTC Products Expand

Physical-contract revenue doubled to $100 million, helped by a $41.7 million contribution from precious metals, while OTC derivatives revenue climbed 87% to $110 million. Listed derivatives and interest and fees on client balances also grew, producing gains across every commercial product line.

Payments Reaches Record Activity

Payments posted record average daily volume of $101 million, up 28%, while net operating revenue increased 18% and segment income advanced 16%. XPay also allowed StoneX to handle high-volume, low-value payments that it had previously rejected because of capacity limits.

Institutional Client Engagement Grows

Institutional listed-derivative contract volumes rose 59% in the quarter and 63% for the year, supported by the full-year contribution from R.J. O’Brien. Average client equity increased 23% quarterly and 73% annually, while securities average daily volume rose 17% year over year.

Record Full-Year Institutional Performance

Despite a difficult fourth quarter, the institutional segment delivered record annual results. Full-year net operating revenue rose 43% to nearly $1.2 billion, while segment income increased 29% to $481 million, with growth across all product lines.

Prime Services Posts Annual Growth

Prime Services generated $122 million of full-year net operating revenue, up 36%, benefiting from organic expansion and acquisitions including R.J. O’Brien and Benchmark. Management also cited continued growth in Europe and other non-U.S. markets.

Derivatives and Physical Revenue Surge

Fourth-quarter listed-derivatives revenue increased 40%, OTC derivatives revenue jumped 88% alongside a 97% rise in contract volume, and physical-contract revenue climbed 89%. Listed-derivative revenue included $143.3 million from R.J. O’Brien, compared with $89.5 million in the comparable post-acquisition period.

Securities Revenue Improves Annually

Securities operating revenue increased 17% year over year, matching a 17% rise in average daily volume. Higher interest income also supported the business during the quarter.

Client Balances Reach $15.5 Billion

Average client equity and FDIC sweep balances totaled $15.5 billion in the fourth quarter, up 24% from a year earlier. The larger balance base remains an important source of scale for StoneX’s platform.

Interest-Rate Hedging Expanded

StoneX added $150 million of fixed-rate SOFR swaps during the quarter, bringing its total swap position to $2.7 billion. The portfolio had an average duration of about 1.4 years and an average rate of 3.57%.

AI Raises Engineering Productivity

Production releases increased about 15% in the first nine months of calendar 2026, while fewer than one in 1,000 changes was reverted. In payments, AI assisted with 75% of changes, subject to AI review and human approval before release.

AI Adoption Accelerates on Platforms

StoneX launched nine products on one digital client platform since April. Client sessions increased 4.5 times between the first and third quarters of fiscal 2026, while the number of platform users grew sixfold.

AI Controls Emphasize Accuracy

A regulatory-reporting assistant achieved 99% to 100% accuracy in testing, while AI agents begin with read-only access and require human approval. StoneX has added security checks, separate agent identities, audit trails and reporting to its risk committee.

Retail and Onboarding Investments

StoneX is expanding self-directed retail through a new multi-asset platform, simpler onboarding and funding, a broader introducing-broker network in Asia-Pacific and rebranding across three jurisdictions. A new onboarding system is designed to make the path from client interest to funded trading faster and easier.

Global Client Ecosystem Scales

StoneX entered fiscal 2027 serving more than 80,000 commercial, institutional and payments clients. It also supported more than 400,000 retail accounts across six continents.

Taxes Reduce Fourth-Quarter Net Income

Fourth-quarter net income fell 2% to $84.2 million despite 10% pretax growth, as year-end adjustments lifted the effective tax rate. Diluted EPS was $0.66.

Sequential Earnings Decline

Net income was 34% below the immediately preceding quarter, while net operating revenue declined 9% sequentially. Institutional and self-directed retail operations were affected by difficult market conditions.

Institutional Segment Faces Pressure

Institutional fourth-quarter net operating revenue fell 13% year over year and segment income dropped 25%. Lower securities revenue and interest and fee income more than offset a $15.9 million increase in listed-derivatives revenue.

Securities Conditions Remain Difficult

Securities revenue declined 17% year over year as rate per million fell 23% amid narrower spreads across equity and fixed-income products. Sequentially, volume fell 10%, rate per million dropped 21% and securities revenue decreased 32%.

Prime Services Quarterly Revenue Falls

Prime Services revenue declined 27% from a strong prior-year quarter and fell 13% from the preceding quarter. The comparison reflected challenging conditions after a particularly strong earlier period.

Self-Directed Retail Weakens

Lower client trading activity pushed fourth-quarter foreign-exchange and contracts-for-difference volume down 17%. Self-directed retail revenue fell 11% and segment income plunged 56%, while sequential declines were 32% and 74%, respectively.

Full-Year Retail Results Trail Prior Year

Self-directed retail generated about $80 million of full-year segment income, down 38% from fiscal 2025. Revenue declined 14%, reflecting weaker activity across the retail franchise.

Retail Activity Stays Subdued

Management linked part of the retail slowdown to subdued market conditions, with the VIX averaging about 16, its lowest quarterly level in two years. The quarter was characterized by both lower trading volume and lower extraction from activity.

FX and CFD Revenue Declines

FX and CFD revenue fell 13% year over year as average daily volume declined 14%, partly offset by a 1% increase in rate per million. Sequentially, revenue dropped 32% as both volume and rate per million fell 18%.

Client Float Income Takes a Hit

Interest and fee income on aggregate client float declined $12.3 million, or 7%, year over year. The quarter included a $17.9 million unrealized mark-to-market loss on investments, compared with a $9 million gain a year earlier.

Compensation and Acquisition Costs Rise

Fixed compensation and other expenses increased $26.2 million, or 9%, including $12 million of acquisition-related costs tied mainly to R.J. O’Brien and Benchmark. Compensation and benefits rose 16% and included $5.1 million of severance and retention costs.

Payments Rate Pressure Offsets Volume

Payments growth was partly offset by a 9% decline in rate per million, despite the 28% increase in average daily volume. Management said onboarding banks and payment companies is gradual, with implementation timelines ranging from nine months to two years.

Guidance and Fiscal 2027 Priorities

StoneX said it remains focused on compounding equity while targeting a 15% return on equity, with another $10 million of R.J. O’Brien expense synergies and $13 million of capital synergies expected in fiscal 2027. Management also expects Prime Services to keep expanding, with two to three significant launches planned, while retail replatforming advances and AI aims to increase delivery faster than costs.

StoneX’s call combined record annual results with a weaker and more volatile fourth quarter. The company is entering the new fiscal year with strong commercial, payments and institutional platforms, while integration benefits, technology investment and retail rebuilding are expected to help address pressure in weaker businesses.
